reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly states that phase-selective recrystallization was achieved, eliminates weak boundaries, triggers strain hardening, and yields ~35% elongation and ~2 GPa true stress in a FCC/B2 EHEA, accurately supporting all key premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can be achieved in eutectic high-entropy alloys by tailored annealing.
PSR eliminates weak internal boundaries in the soft phase that cause dislocation pile-ups.
Eliminating these boundaries reduces local stress concentrations and microcrack initiation.
The hard phase skeleton is preserved during PSR, maintaining strength.
PSR treatment yields ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress in a FCC/B2 EHEA.
